pathdreamer.title: Pathdreamer: A World Model for Indoor Navigation
pathdreamer.authors: Jing Yu Koh; Honglak Lee; Yinfei Yang; Jason Baldridge; Peter Anderson
pathdreamer.problem: Predict indoor panoramic RGB/depth/semantics at a specified future pose from observed RGB-D, semantic labels and pose history. Downstream planning assumes known future navigation graph geometry.
pathdreamer.mechanism: Section 3 pp. 3–5: accumulate a 3D point cloud and reproject into candidate pose. Stochastic RedNet structure generator inpaints semantics/depth with 32-channel Gaussian latent, conditional prior and ground-truth-conditioned posterior. Semantic CE/depth L1/KL weights 1/100/.5. Stage 2 MultiSPADE generates RGB conditioned on completed structure, RGB guidance and prior frame, using GAN hinge, perceptual and feature-matching losses. Stages train separately; RGB training receives ground-truth structure. About 400 k random 5–8 node MP3D trajectories; structure 512×256, RGB 1024×512. Quantitative inference uses prior mean. Beam search ranks imagined trajectories by instruction compatibility, executes first action and replans from a new real observation.
pathdreamer.novelty: Hierarchical geometry-guided stochastic completion replaces repeated-current-view lookahead. Prediction is independent of a specific policy and distinct from auxiliary-training-only semantics.
pathdreamer.results: Table 1 p. 7 unseen semantic mIoU 78.3 one-step versus 50.8 over 1–6 steps. Table 3 p. 8 horizon 3 navigation SR 50.4/SPL 47.3 versus repetition 40.6/37.7 and oracle future images 59.3/55.8. The ground-truth future navigation graph is provided throughout: visual oracle-gap reduction is not evidence of planning without oracle geometry.
pathdreamer.bottleneck: Hallucinated structure compounds with horizon; ground-truth structure during RGB training introduces stage mismatch. Multi-stage high-resolution synthesis costs compute; stochasticity and GAN realism do not imply calibrated uncertainty.
pathdreamer.followups: DREAMWALKER predicts future waypoints, HNR renders features cheaply, SALI stores imagined nodes. These partly address geometry/computation/persistence but do not verify hidden-world truth.

vlnsig.title: Improving Vision-and-Language Navigation by Generating Future-View Image Semantics
vlnsig.problem: Improve HAMT/DUET representations through semantic image-token prediction in graphVLN. This is auxiliary training, not online imagined search.
vlnsig.mechanism: Section 3 pp. 3–5: frozen dVAE supplies 8192-token distributions over 16 pixel patches; mean, sampled or weighted distributions provide targets. HAMT adds masked-trajectory (MTM), masked-panorama (MPM) and action-conditioned future-image-semantic (APIG) tasks. Whole-image masking supports cached CLIP features. Weighted-patch heads condition on patch weights. Dynamic 1000-token vocabulary follows EMA frequency and difficulty (Eq. 6); soft-target CE/KL (Eqs.7–9) trains prediction. Finetuning retains IL/RL plus APIG. DUET omits MTM due to different history encoding. Inference uses the trained backbone without decoded future images or rollout planning.
vlnsig.novelty: Prediction targets preserve more visual-token semantics than a single pooled feature; weighted-patch identifiability is a mathematical target property under rich weighting, not a finite-SGD guarantee.
vlnsig.results: Table 1 p. 6 HAMT unseen SR 66→68,SPL 61→62; test 65/60 unchanged. DUET test 69/59→72/60. Table 2 task baseline 64.4/58.8 versus all 68.1/62.3. Results support regularization with split-dependent gains.
vlnsig.bottleneck: Token targets can prioritize common visual content rather than action-critical details; pretrained dVAE/CLIP and dynamic vocabulary determine information retained. No causal intervention establishes that deployment decisions rely on correct future predictions.
vlnsig.followups: MonoDream and FantasyVLN also use training-only prediction; NavQ supplies inference-time future semantic graphs; VisualImaginations supplies generated landmark prototypes.
associated: VLN-SIG (supplement).pdf, pp. 1–3: objectives, weighted-patch argument, hyperparameters and additional evaluations.
vlnsig.access: Supplement p. 2 gives dynamic vocabulary size 1000, frequency/difficulty weights gamma=1 and lambda=0.5, task-mixture/masking settings, and about 30 hours on two A6000 GPUs. Its weighted-patch result assumes equality over sufficiently rich weights and a linear decomposition; it is not a finite-optimization guarantee. Supplement p. 3 decodes visual examples retaining 70% ground-truth tokens, so these images do not demonstrate autonomous future-image synthesis. No benchmark was executed.

visualimaginations.title: Do Visual Imaginations Improve Vision-and-Language Navigation Agents?
visualimaginations.authors: Akhil Perincherry; Jacob Krantz; Stefan Lee
visualimaginations.problem: Add generated visual landmark exemplars to HAMT/DUET R2R inputs. These are text-conditioned prototypes, not predictions of an unseen actual camera state.
visualimaginations.mechanism: Section 3 pp. 3–4: FG-R2R segments yield spaCy noun phrases filtered by a manual exclusion list; SDXL renders real-estate-style landmark imagery. ViT features, type embeddings and a three-layerMLP align images with text; imagination tokens join instruction tokens in HAMT and DUET branches. Auxiliary cosine alignment to noun-phrase embeddings (Eq. 2) and three-stage finetuning train new projections, then backbone at lowLR, then jointly. Deployment consumes cached/generated instruction images without an action-conditioned transition model. p. 5 reports 41,558 training images,1024 square and 3.2 sec/image onH100.
visualimaginations.novelty: Explicit visual prototypes aid linguistic grounding, contrasting with VLN-SIG prediction supervision and Pathdreamer environment-conditioned rendering.
visualimaginations.results: Table 1 p. 5 HAMT unseen 66.24/61.51→67.26/62.02, test 65/60 unchanged; DUET unseen 71.52/60.41→72.12/60.48, test 69/59→71/60. Modest improvements require matched multi-seed assessment. Generator pretraining and preprocessing add data/compute. Table 3, p. 6: removing imaginations at test time still gives SR 66.92 versus baseline 66.24, while correct imaginations give 67.26 and wrong ones 66.24. This directly supports a training regularization component plus a smaller aligned-input benefit. Table 6, p. 7 compares no auxiliary loss (66.75 SR), InfoNCE (67.18) and cosine alignment (67.26); the loss choice has modest effects. Selected attention visualizations explicitly do not establish causality.
visualimaginations.bottleneck: Prototype specificity can mislead unusual appearances; parser/manual exclusions restrict coverage. Images add semantic priors but cannot reveal hidden physical facts. Gains may reflect regularization/priming rather than grounded foresight.
visualimaginations.followups: MonoDream/FantasyVLN shift prediction into training. Compare prototype grounding separately from actual-state and action-conditioned prediction.

nwm.title: Navigation World Models
nwm.authors: Amir Bar; Gaoyue Zhou; Danny Tran; Trevor Darrell; Yann LeCun
nwm.problem: Goal-image navigation and action-conditioned video prediction over heterogeneous robot datasets; no route-language input.
nwm.mechanism: Section 3: a Stable Diffusion VAE encodes RGB images. CDiT processes target patches with self-attention and historical context with cross-attention; its interaction cost scales approximately as O(m n² d) for m context frames, n patches and width d, instead of self-attention over all concatenated frames. Four historical frames, displacement/yaw action and signed time offset up to 16 seconds condition adaptive layer normalization. Training uses clean-latent denoising MSE plus a variance variational-bound term. Actions are normalized by robot step size; actionless Ego4D data can supply temporal supervision. At inference CEM or reranking uses generated endpoint similarity to a goal image. The largest 1B-parameter training uses 64 H100 GPUs and batch 4096. The inspected released CEM planner restricts candidate trajectories more than an unconstrained sequence optimizer; see code audit.
nwm.novelty: Cross-context diffusion with action/time conditioning supports flexible generative horizons and goal-image planning. It generates pixels, unlike DINO-WM's feature-only planner, and uses substantially larger visual priors/data than PlaNet without learning a task reward.
nwm.results: Table 1, p. 6: LPIPS is 0.760 with time only, 0.318 with action only and 0.295 with both. Table 2, p. 7: RECON two-second ATE/RPE is 1.13/0.35 versus NoMaD 1.93/0.52; reranking 32 proposals gives 1.78/0.48. These are offline trajectory errors, not measured physical success or collision guarantees.
nwm.bottleneck: Diffusion×CEM is costly; endpoint metrics and unsupported action rollouts can be exploited. Logged action/time dependence does not identify all interventions. OfficialREADME notes nonredistributable high-resolution SACSoN/HuRoN data, limiting exact reproduction.
nwm.followups: Vid2World adapts pretrained video generators to causal action conditioning; LCVN adds language, actor–critic learning and unified prediction. Their datasets and evaluation protocols differ.

genex.title: GenEx: Generating an Explorable World
genex.authors: Taiming Lu; Tianmin Shu; Alan Yuille; Daniel Khashabi; Jieneng Chen
genex.problem: Imagine panoramic exploration from a partial view and use imagined perspectives in embodiedQA, including multi-agent perspective-taking.
genex.mechanism: Sections 3–4 adapt Stable Video Diffusion to panoramic exploration. The system first rotates the sphere geometrically, then generates a forward video segment. The spherical-consistency objective (Eq. 2) decodes generated latents, rotates predicted and target panoramas together, re-encodes them and penalizes their latent difference alongside ordinary diffusion loss. An LLM proposes orientation/distance and reasons over generated views. GenEx-DB contains four synthetic visual styles; Street View and Behavior Vision Suite provide held-out domains. Equation 4 describes belief updates using imagined observations, but a calibrated posterior-inference algorithm is not established. Generated views are samples from the model conditioned on available evidence; they are not additional camera measurements.
genex.novelty: The contribution combines panoramic video exploration, spherical consistency and an embodied-QA benchmark. It targets coherent imagined perspective-taking rather than a learned navigation action policy.
genex.results: Table 1, p. 8: FVD is 69.5 for the full method, 81.9 without spherical consistency and 196.7 for six-view generation. IELC measures Inception-feature error after 1,000 closed imagined loops. Table 2, p. 9 gives 0.105 on street scenes and 0.092 indoors, so a blanket claim that both are below 0.1 is inaccurate. GenEx-EQA contains more than 200 synthetic scenarios and uses GPT-4 o as a judge for logic scoring. These are generated-world/QA evaluations, not R2R success or physical navigation deployment.
genex.bottleneck: DEDUCTION: conditional on a fixed real history and model, self-generated samples add computation but no independent observational information about the actual hidden state. Counting them as independent likelihood evidence can create unwarranted certainty. A consistently false generated world can satisfy loop closure. Facts about an occluded physical hazard require a real observation or an explicitly justified prior.
genex.followups: SALI, ImagineNav, Pathdreamer and WorldVLN differ in their interfaces between real and imagined evidence. A useful research gap concerns provenance and decision reliability, rather than the mere ability to retain or lengthen generation.

imaginenav.title: ImagineNav: Prompting Vision-Language Models as Embodied Navigator through Scene Imagination
imaginenav.authors: Xinxin Zhao; Wenzhe Cai; Likun Tang; Teng Wang
imaginenav.problem: Open-vocabulary ObjectNav on HM3D/HSSD using a VLM without object-specific fine-tuning. The complete pipeline still contains trained waypoint and PointNav modules.
imaginenav.mechanism: Section 3: Where2Imagine uses ResNet18 and human ObjectNav demonstrations to predict displacement/orientation proposals. Six panoramic RGB directions and depth filter candidate views using wall-distance and rotation constraints. PolyOculus novel-view synthesis renders candidates; GPT-4o mini chooses an indexed image for the target object; pretrained VER PointNav executes and replans after arrival. Training includes Habitat-Web demonstrations. No persistent semantic map is maintained. The full system requires depth, despite introductory RGB-only descriptions.
imaginenav.novelty: The VLM chooses among predicted candidate views supported by learned waypoint proposals. This differs from prompting only on currently observed views.
imaginenav.results: Table 1, p. 7: HM3D SR 53/SPL 23.8 versus VLFM 52.5/30.4; HSSD 51/24.9. Oracle views raise SR to 62/59. Table 2, p. 8 compares learned versus fixed waypoints on 100 episodes: 56/24.3 versus 49/23.3. That smaller ablation differs from the 200-episode headline setting. Better success is not necessarily better path efficiency.
imaginenav.bottleneck: NVS domain shift and proposal constraints limit useful branching. Mapless local choices can revisit regions. Open-vocabulary is not training-free, and predictor realism is not calibrated outcome reliability.
imaginenav.followups: ImagineNav++ (arXiv 2512.17435) adds selective foveation and memory: https://200203z.github.io/imaginenav-plus/ . Its recorded repository remains a forthcoming-code page. WMNav instead stores heuristic curiosity scores.

monodream.title: MonoDream: Monocular Vision-Language Navigation with Panoramic Dreaming
monodream.authors: Shuo Wang; Yongcai Wang; Zhaoxin Fan; Yucheng Wang; Maiyue Chen; Kaihui Wang; Zhizhong Su; Wanting Li; Xudong Cai; Yeying Jin; Deying Li
monodream.problem: Monocular RGB VLN-CE with eight historical frames. Panoramic RGB and depth are privileged training targets.
monodream.mechanism: The NVILA-lite 2 B backbone (SigLIP plus Qwen2) outputs a unified state h_t. Four mean-squared-error terms (Eq. 5) align h_t-derived predictions with current and future panoramic RGB/depth features. Panoramas use four cube-map views; depth is log-scaled and colorized. The agent predicts the next three actions with cross-entropy (Eq. 6) and reconstructs the instruction with cross-entropy (Eq. 7), optimizing their weighted sum (Eq. 8). Projection and pooling dimensions are incompletely specified. Training uses five epochs on eight H20 GPUs, batch 80 and learning rate 1 e-5, with 320,000 R2R steps, 600,000 RxR steps and 500,000 DAgger steps. Auxiliary heads are disabled at inference, so deployment has no imagined rollout or search. The authors' claim of no external data concerns additional navigation fine-tuning data, not the foundation models' pretraining.
monodream.novelty: Privileged geometric, panoramic and future supervision improves a monocular representation. This extends the training-supervision role seen in VLN-SIG and differs from DREAMWALKER's online generation.
monodream.results: The main R2R result is SR 55.8/SPL 49.1. RxR is 49.4/40.9 versus NaVILA 49.3/44.0, so the method does not obtain the highest SPL . Table 5, p. 7, on the smaller ablation training setting: current-depth-only SR is 42.2, future-depth-only 39.8, and the full method 46.1. Table 6 shows decreasing SR with prediction horizon: one step 39.1, two steps 34.3, three steps 29.2. Table 7 reports 0.8 seconds per step on a 4090 versus 1.2 seconds for 8 B baselines, but model size differs.
monodream.bottleneck: Longer prediction supervision can hurt under partial observability. Current geometry/panoramic information may explain more of the gain than foresight. The model has no deployment confidence-calibration or observed-residual correction mechanism. No independently executed experiment establishes transfer beyond the reported protocol.
monodream.followups: FantasyVLN also uses imagination mainly during training; NavForesee retains predicted semantic/depth structures in action computation. Comparisons must match sensing, data and backbone size.
monodream.access: An initially inaccessible project page did not establish absence of code. A later primary-source search identified the official MonoDream implementation in HorizonRobotics/RoboOrchardLab, with author/checkpoint links in its project README. The final dossier records inspected inference/model/preprocessing/evaluation files and the absence of the complete auxiliary-training pipeline from that project listing.

navforesee.title: NavForesee: A Unified Vision-Language World Model for Hierarchical Planning and Dual-Horizon Navigation Prediction
navforesee.authors: Fei Liu; Shichao Xie; Minghua Luo; Zedong Chu; Junjun Hu; Xiaolong Wu; Mu Xu
navforesee.problem: RGB VLN-CE using observation history and relative pose, with hierarchical instruction planning and continuous waypoint chunks.
navforesee.mechanism: Section 3: Qwen2.5-VL 3 B predicts planning text and two sets of future queries: a fixed short horizon and a longer milestone horizon. Gemini 2.5 Pro annotates 10,000 R2R and 20,000 RxR episodes; 16.7% of poor terminal milestones are filtered, leaving about 0.2 million and 1.3 million steps. Structured attention lets long-horizon queries see short-horizon queries, separates semantic/depth branches and lets action queries see all of them. Heads predict DINO/SAM semantic features with MSE and depth with scale-invariant logarithmic loss. An inverse-dynamics head predicts K×5 waypoint vectors (x, y, sin (theta), cos (theta), stop) with MSE; planning text uses cross-entropy. These are goal-conditioned future targets and inverse action prediction, not clearly candidate-action-conditioned counterfactual simulation. New real observations refresh each control cycle, but no calibrated observed-residual objective is specified.
navforesee.novelty: Combines hierarchical language planning with two-horizon semantic/geometric prediction. Planning-only and prediction-only controls are necessary to distinguish its contribution from HNR, NavMorph and MonoDream.
navforesee.results: Table 1, p. 7: R2R SR 66.2/SPL 59.7 versus CorrectNav 65.1/62.3; RxR 66.3/53.2 versus 69.3/63.3. Table 2 gives 66.2/59.7 for the full system, 48.8/39.4 without VLM planning and 58.6/50.1 without long-horizon prediction. Table 3 gives short-horizon SR 66.2 at five steps, 64.1 at four and 56.5 at three. Ablations support the internal recipe, while the headline comparisons do not show uniform superiority.
navforesee.bottleneck: Predicted futures may act as goal templates rather than faithful consequences of alternative actions. Teacher annotation and filtering add cost and data selection. Qualitative geometric fidelity does not validate confidence. No official implementation was verified.
navforesee.followups: WorldVLN and LCVN unify action/observation prediction differently. SC²-WM adds delayed observed-residual adaptation as well as immediate internal refinement; those mechanisms must be distinguished from simple anticipation.

fantasyvln.title: FantasyVLN: Unified Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Vision-and-Language Navigation
fantasyvln.authors: Jing Zuo; Lingzhou Mu; Fan Jiang; Chengcheng Ma; Mu Xu; Yonggang Qi
fantasyvln.problem: Long, multistage LH-VLN with a 7 B VLM. The aim is to benefit from reasoning supervision while using a fast direct action mode at deployment.
fantasyvln.mechanism: The backbone supports four gated modes: direct non-CoT, textual CoT, coarse VAR visual CoT, and combined multimodal CoT. The VAR decoder is frozen. Equations 4–8 alternate direct action cross-entropy with cross-mode alignment. After a non-CoT update, its detached action-token probabilities supervise CoT action outputs, while ordinary token losses supervise the reasoning content. Thus the explicit alignment direction is not simply a CoT teacher distilled into a direct student. Shared backbone updates may still improve the direct mode. Deployment primarily selects non-CoT inference, making visual imagination chiefly a training mechanism; the code audit below confirms the alternating update order.
fantasyvln.novelty: Unified reasoning modes and action alignment provide auxiliary learning for a fast direct policy. CoT-VLA instead generates intermediate images during deployment. Auxiliary reasoning supervision and shared-backbone transfer are close prior mechanisms that constrain broad novelty claims.
fantasyvln.results: Table 1, p. 6: full-task SR 2.44, ISR 11.01, CSR 9.64 and CGT 8.99, versus Aux-Think SR 0.65 and baseline SR 0. Table 2 reports 1.03 actions per second versus CoT-VLA 0.19 (about 5.4 times faster) and WorldVLA 1.02. Table 3 gives visual-only non-CoT ISR 11.19, slightly above the full system's 11.01, although the full system has better complete-task SR . Removing alignment gives SR 0. CoT-VLA and Aux-Think were reimplemented because their original code was unavailable, limiting direct comparability.
fantasyvln.bottleneck: More than 97% of full tasks still fail. Token alignment does not prove that reasoning is faithful or causally responsible for actions; auxiliary branches may provide representation regularization. Foundation-model priors, scale and training data complicate attribution.
fantasyvln.followups: MonoDream disables auxiliary heads at inference. NavForesee and WorldVLN retain predicted structures in action computation. Grouping these papers by actual deployment use is more informative than grouping by the word imagination.

worldvln.title: WorldVLN: Autoregressive World Action Model for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
worldvln.authors: Baining Zhao; Jiacheng Xu; Weicheng Feng; Xin Zhang; Zhaolu Wang; Haoyang Wang; Shilong Ji; Ziyou Wang; Jianjie Fang; Zhiheng Zheng; Weichen Zhang; Yu Shang; Wei Wu; Chen Gao; Xinlei Chen; Yong Li
worldvln.problem: Aerial language navigation with four-dimensional displacement/yaw waypoints. The task differs from ground-based R2R-CE.
worldvln.mechanism: An InfinityStar latent autoregressive video model predicts the next segment from language and real observation history. A Wan VAE and TSformer visual-odometry initialization support action decoding. The system executes a segment, then replaces its imagined history with newly encoded real video (Eqs. 3–6). Stage one combines visual likelihood with action regression (Eqs. 7–8). Stage two uses online GRPO with trajectory-closeness, terminal-distance and reference-action likelihood rewards (Eqs. 9–13). Training uses eight 80 GB A800 GPUs and simulation uses a 4090. Mathematical caveat: multiplying all rewards in a per-time-step group by the same positive gamma^(j−1) cancels in standardized advantages (Eq. 13), apart from epsilon. Early-step weighting therefore needs an additional noncancelling weight or a different grouping. The continuous-action likelihood used by GRPO also requires implementation specification.
worldvln.novelty: Integrates generated visual/action sequences, navigation reinforcement learning and periodic replacement by real history. Unlike training-only imagination, generated segments affect execution; unlike a fully observed controller, feedback is delayed until the segment ends.
worldvln.results: Table 1 reports average SR 79.12/78.02 for fixed/open UAVFlow instructions. Table 2 gives indoor SR 41.76/nDTW 13.48 versus pi 0 27.16/9.44. On the easy subset nDTW 13.04 is below pi 0 14.52. These are author-reported aerial-navigation experiments, not executed reproduction or ground-navigation results.
worldvln.bottleneck: Segmented execution delays correction. Reinforcement learning can exploit model or reward inaccuracies. The reward-scale cancellation is a scoped deduction that requires reconciliation with the unreleased trainer. The official snapshot is a project page, so actual action likelihoods, optimization and evaluation code remain unavailable.
worldvln.followups: NWM, LCVN, CoT-VLA and Vid2World are close mechanistic comparisons. Real-observation assimilation must be separated from internal feedback computed only from predictions.
